ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Given \( f(t) \) and \( g(t) \) as shown below, what is the Laplace transform of \( g(t) \)?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The g(t) image on the right side of the attached figure shows that the signal jumps from 0 to 1 at t=3, and jumps back from 1 to 0 at t=5; therefore g(t) is a unit-height rectangular pulse from t=3 to t=5, and is 0 at all other times. Reasoning: From the image it can be written as g(t)=0 (t<3), g(t)=1 (3\le t\le 5), g(t)=0 (t>5). According to the definition of the Laplace transform, G(s)=\int_0^\infty g(t)e^{-st}dt. Since g(t) is equal to 1 only on [3,5], G(s)=\int_3^5 e^{-st}dt=[-e^{-st}/s]_3^5=(e^{-3s}-e^{-5s})/s=\frac{e^{-3s}}{s}(1-e^{-2s}).
